paper.title: Online switching control with stability and regret guarantees

settings.name_in_paper: Online switching control with a finite candidate controller pool (single trajectory, unknown nonlinear dynamics, unknown time-varying costs, bandit feedback)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Online control of an unknown nonlinear dynamical system with state: costs depend on the state trajectory induced by past controller choices (MDP-like control problem rather than a stateless bandit).
unmapped: arms are black-box candidate controllers; costs c_t(x_t,u_t) depend on the system state, which depends on all past controller selections (unbounded memory)
some controllers may be destabilizing, so costs are unbounded; at least one controller is E-ISS and delta-ES with parameters (kappa, rho, beta)
the learner knows the stability parameters (kappa, rho, beta) and the noise bound w_max
process noise w_t bounded by w_max and obliviously adversarial
dynamics L_f-Lipschitz with f(0,0,0)=0; controllers L_pi-Lipschitz; costs locally Lipschitz (Assumption 3) with 0 <= c_t(0,0) <= c_0
regret is against the best controller in the set B of controllers satisfying E-ISS and delta-ES
settings.definition_quote: We consider an unknown nonlinear dynamical system $x_{t+1}=f(x_t, u_t, w_t)$ and unknown time-varying cost functions $c_t(x_t, u_t)$ ... We consider a \textit{bandit} setting, i.e., we can only observe the value of $c_t(x_t, u_t)$ after observing $x_t$ and implementing $u_t$ at stage $t$. ... We consider a finite pool of candidate controllers

bound.expression_latex: \alpha_4 \eta NT + (\alpha_5 \eta N\gamma^{4\mathbb M} +\alpha_6  \gamma^{2\mathbb M})\textup{poly}(\|x_0\|,  \bar \pi_0) + \tau\log N/\eta +\alpha_7 J

symbols.M_bad: number of candidate controllers not satisfying E-ISS (paper's \mathbb M)
symbols.P_x0: a polynomial in ||x_0|| and bar pi_0
symbols.alpha_4: polynomial constant in L_f, L_c1, L_c2, c_0, L_pi, kappa, beta w_max, 1/(1-rho), 1/(1-2^{3/4} kappa rho^tau)

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: at least one controller E-ISS and delta-ES with known (kappa,rho,beta); Lipschitz dynamics/controllers; locally Lipschitz costs
comparator restricted to controllers satisfying E-ISS and delta-ES

source.label: thm: policy regret bdd
source.quote: When $\tau \geq \frac{\log(2\sqrt 2 \kappa)}{-\log \rho}$ and $\eta_j=\eta$,  Exp3-ISS's  regret satisfies PolicyRegret \leq \alpha_4 \eta NT + (\alpha_5 \eta N\gamma^{4\mathbb M} +\alpha_6  \gamma^{2\mathbb M})\textup{poly}(\|x_0\|,  \bar \pi_0) + \tau\log N/\eta +\alpha_7 J where $\gamma = L_f(1+L_{\pi})\kappa$, $\alpha_4, \dots, \alpha_7$ are  polynomials of ...

results.notes: Paper's N (number of controllers) mapped to K. Expectation over algorithm randomness; noise is oblivious adversarial.

symbols.M_bad: number of candidate controllers not satisfying E-ISS (paper's \mathbb M)

tuning: tau = max(T^{1/3} N^{-1/3}, log(2 sqrt 2 kappa)/(-log rho))

source.label: cor: regret bdd order
source.quote: Let $\eta=O(\frac{1}{N^{2/3} T^{1/3}})$ and $\tau=\max(T^{1/3}N^{-1/3}, \frac{\log(2\sqrt 2 \kappa)}{-\log \rho})$. When $T\geq N$,  we have $$\textup{PolicyRegret}\leq   \tilde O( N^{1/3}  T^{2/3})+ \exp(O(\mathbb M)), $$ where $\tilde O(\cdot)$ hides a $\log(N)$ factor.

results.notes: The second term is exp(O(M)) in the paper; the constant inside the exponent cannot be expressed, so exp(M_bad) is a placeholder. Tilde hides log(N).

symbols.M_bad: number of controllers not satisfying E-ISS

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (only an E-ISS controller is needed per Remark 5)

source.label: thm: finite gain stability
source.quote: When  $\tau \geq \frac{\log(2\sqrt 2 \kappa)}{-\log \rho}$,  Algorithm \ref{alg: exp3 iss} is finite-gain $l_1$ stable: $\sum_{t=0}^T \|x_t\|\leq  \beta w_{\max} (T+ \alpha_1 J) +\alpha_2 (L_f (1+L_{\pi}) \kappa)^{\mathbb M}\|x_0\|+ \alpha_3 (L_f (1+L_{\pi}) \kappa)^{\mathbb M}(\beta w_{\max}+\bar \pi_0),$

results.notes: Bound on cumulative state norm sum_t ||x_t|| (finite-gain l1 stability), not a regret. Holds for every realization. Theorem also gives an O(.) l2 stability bound, not recorded separately.

cited_results.cited_title: Bandits with switching costs: T 2/3 regret
cited_results.setting_description: Multi-armed bandit with memory / switching costs, policy regret; N^{1/3}T^{2/3} shown to be the optimal regret order
